all_found.desc: [BUG] With a partly read scope (branch name read, a later scope git call failed), blocksHere is true for every row, so the unguarded StatusOverridden dedupe leg lets another branch's granted override absorb this named branch's re-raise. branch-a's finding is override-granted; branch-b (from main) re-raises it during a transient git failure: no row is written, OpenFindings=0 and that task-done passes; once git recovers branch-b has no blocker. Verified in a scratch clone at 28cdee1.

[ADVISORY] A legacy row absorbed via PastHead is never moved forward, so after a rebase and git's 30-day reflog expiry its head falls out of the reflog and ancestry and it reads Orphaned. pr-ready passes the branch with the defect until task-done re-raises it.

[ADVISORY] Three partly-read-scope tests restore the loadScope stub with a plain assignment rather than t.Cleanup/defer. A t.Fatal inside reconcileOn leaves the stub installed and cascades misleading failures.

findings.issue_text: [BUG] With a partly read scope (branch name read, a later scope git call failed), blocksHere is true for every row, so the unguarded StatusOverridden dedupe leg lets another branch's granted override absorb this named branch's re-raise. branch-a's finding is override-granted; branch-b (from main) re-raises it during a transient git failure: no row is written, OpenFindings=0 and that task-done passes; once git recovers branch-b has no blocker. Verified in a scratch clone at 28cdee1.

[ADVISORY] If symbolic-ref itself fails on a checked-out branch, Current is empty and the run takes the detached path (dedupes against every row), contrary to the comment's 'named run with a failed scope read dedupes only against its own rows'. The re-raise stays attributed to another branch's row (verdict still blocks under the unknown scope); the comment overstates.
